There's a long-running joke that Apple announces each new iPhone Pro as 'the best iPhone we've ever made' as if that's some kind of surprise.

Specifically, we expect to see another step towards the 'one piece of glass' vision next year, bringing an end to a decade of incremental changes…

The evolution of the iPhone Pro lineup

If you line up every iPhone from the 12 Pro to the 16 Pro, I think many people would struggle to tell them apart visually, apart from the switch from the notch to the Dynamic Island in 2022. The 17 Pro was only a slight exception thanks to its elongated camera module and the cosmic orange colour.

Of course, every model brings new features, but I think it's fair to say here that unless a particular feature is especially useful to you personally, you really need to skip at least two or three generations to make the upgrade worthwhile in terms of a noticeably better experience.

This is absolutely not a criticism of Apple. The fact is, the smartphone is a mature technology, at least in terms of conventional design. We don't see huge differences between adjacent generations because there's just so little room left to improve each year.

Apple is now experimenting with different designs, starting with the iPhone Air, and of course the iPhone Duo – and we expect another major design leap next year, in the form of a 20th anniversary model.

Exactly how Apple will position next year's design remains a little unclear. There was initially talk of it being a standalone model, separate from the iPhone 19 Pro, but other reports have suggested it will be next year's Pro model. There's also the question of whether Apple will use consecutive numbering or skip a number to mark the milestone, so it might be called the iPhone 20 Pro.

Personally, I do expect it to be the new iPhone Pro design, regardless of whether Apple calls it 19 or 20. If so, the iPhone 18 Pro will be the final iteration of a look that has lasted for six or seven years.

I'm jumping two generations from the iPhone 16 Pro, so I'll list separately the features that are new to me with each yearly model. I'll skip improvements I consider unimportant or of no use to me at all, like the move from a 6-core GPU to a 7-core GPU and GenLock.

iPhone 17 Pro features carried forward

  • Center Stage front camera for photos and video calls
  • Ultra-stable video
  • Dual-shot video
  • Telephoto lens upgraded from 5x to 8x
  • Telephoto sensor upgraded from 12MP to 48MP
  • ProRes RAW video
  • Better battery life
  • Faster charging

iPhone 18 Pro new features

  • Wider maximum aperture on the main lens
  • Variable aperture on the main lens
  • Pro camera controls (aperture, shutter speed, white balance, histogram)
  • Photographic Styles third generation
  • Smart focus tracking
  • Cinematic effects added to standard video
  • Tap-to-zoom and rotation for front camera
  • Smaller Dynamic Island that can display three live activities simultaneously
  • (Even) longer battery life
  • (Even) faster charging

My personal… highlights

For me personally, at this stage I'll be focusing on five features.

Variable aperture lens

Although the showstopper is the variable aperture lens, I've said before that perhaps we shouldn't expect too much from it. The maximum aperture is only slightly wider on what is still a tiny sensor, so I wouldn't expect to see much difference in shallow depth-of-field effects.

That said, the wider maximum aperture does let in more light, roughly the equivalent of two-thirds of a stop. How much of a difference that makes in practice remains to be seen, but in theory it should mean shorter exposure times in Night mode. Since I use this feature a lot, often still shooting handheld, I'm very much looking forward to trying it out.

Pro camera controls

Being able to control shutter speed will definitely be useful for subjects like panning shots. Full control over white balance is sure to be helpful too. I also expect the histogram will be very useful when setting exposure manually.

I'm not generally someone who likes using filters, whether when shooting or editing afterwards on the iPhone, preferring traditional adjustments. So I rarely use the existing Photographic Styles and don't expect to use this latest version much either. But I have to say I'm quite intrigued by its film settings, so I'll definitely give it a try.

One of the biggest weaknesses of autofocus when shooting video is when the subject is briefly obscured by another object, and the camera may shift focus to that obstruction. Smart focus tracking claims to solve this problem, so I'll definitely be giving it a thorough testing.

Cinematic effects in standard video

Top liked comment, from atonaldenim

I'm really looking forward to hearing your thoughts after using the 18 Pro. I personally need a new phone soon, and I'm still using my 12 Mini. (RIP Mini.)

The telephoto lens would be a treat, one that might let me accept how much heavier and bigger the phone is than the Mini. I'm currently weighing up whether to pay the full $1,200 for a new 18 Pro, or pick up a second-hand 16 Pro for around $700 or less, which seems to be roughly the going rate these days.

(The 17 Pro and 18 Pro are still pretty close in price, so I'm not considering the 17 Pro – I'd rather spend a bit more and get the 18 Pro.)

So if you feel the 18 Pro represents a significant step up over the 16 Pro in the areas you mention, I'd be very interested to know. Thanks!

I said less than two months ago that Apple seemed to have abandoned Cinematic video mode. I noted that was a shame, because if Cinematic Mode video was done well, it would be an absolute killer feature for anyone wanting to use their iPhone as a more serious video camera. To date, the feature works, but there's always something missing; it never quite gets there.

But it looks like I was wrong: one of the new features of the iPhone 18 is the ability to apply cinematic video effects to footage shot in standard mode.

It's certainly convenient no longer having to decide in advance whether to use the mode or not, but what interests me most is that Apple is paying attention to the feature again. This suggests they've invested resources in it, so we can expect it to continue improving, much as Portrait mode did for photography in its early days. I'm really looking forward to testing it.

These are the features I think are likely to make the biggest difference to me personally. What about you? If you've already upgraded to the iPhone 18 Pro, which features were it that prompted you to upgrade? Feel free to share in the comments.
